description: Windowed hierarchical cooperative A\* (WHCA\*) plans many agents in rounds over a reservation table that reaches only a window of `w` steps ahead. Every round, all agents plan from where they stand, one after another, each avoiding the window plans of the agents before it; the first agent rotates (agent `r mod n` in round `r`), so an agent that had to make way goes first in a later round. Beyond the window an agent ignores the others and follows its distance table to the goal. Then every agent executes the first `k` steps of its plan, `1 ≤ k ≤ w` (16 and 8 by default, half the window, as Silver suggests), and the next round replans. The window is also how it handles stale information: the others' plans are trusted only through the window, and the agents sync again before that trust runs out. Within a round the window plans are pairwise conflict-free, so the executed plan is too. The run ends at the first round that starts with every agent at its goal. It has no quality guarantee and is not complete: agents can oscillate forever, so always pass a budget of rounds.
